# Jubilees Chapter 12 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 12:3 — "mute forms" vs. "dumb forms"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "dumb forms, and a misleading of the heart" | "Dumb" = unable to speak |
| LOGOS | "mute forms and a delusion of the heart" | "Mute" replaces archaic "dumb" |
| PNEUMA | "silent objects — they confuse the people who trust them" | Paraphrase; "confuse" for "delusion" |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Mute" is the modern equivalent of archaic "dumb" (speechless). "Delusion" is more precise than PNEUMA's "confuse" for the Ge'ez term of heart-deception.

---

## 12:14 — "two weeks of years" — rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "two weeks of years" | Jubilees calendrical unit |
| LOGOS | "two weeks of years" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "fourteen years" | Renders the number directly |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Two weeks of years" is the Jubilees technical expression; converting to "fourteen years" (PNEUMA) loses the calendrical vocabulary of the text.

---

## 12:17 — Abram's astronomical realization

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "All the signs of the stars, and the signs of the moon and of the sun are all in the hand of the LORD. Why do I search them out?" | Full rhetorical question |
| LOGOS | "All the signs of the stars, and the signs of the moon and the sun — all are in the hand of the LORD. Why am I searching them out?" | Same with slight restructuring |
| PNEUMA | "'All of this — the stars, the moon, the sun — all of it is in God's hands. So why am I studying it?'" | Compressed; "So why" adds inference |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The full enumeration (stars, moon, sun) is important — it covers the three categories of Chaldean divination that Abram has just been practicing. PNEUMA's compression loses this.

---

## 12:24 — "through me" — the angel identifies itself

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a word of the LORD was sent to him through me, saying" | Literal; "me" = the angel-narrator |
| LOGOS | "a word of the LORD was sent to him through me, saying" | Same — strong agreement |
| PNEUMA | "the word of the LORD came to him through me, the angel, saying" | Adds "the angel" as gloss |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Through me" is sufficient; PNEUMA's "the angel" is an editorial clarification that is not in the source. The reader should infer the narrator's identity from the established context.

---

## 12:31 — Botanical catalog of the Promised Land

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "vines and figs and pomegranates, oaks and ilexes, and terebinths and oil trees and cedars..." | Full list with "and" connectors |
| LOGOS | "vines and figs and pomegranates, oaks and ilex, terebinths and olive trees, cedars and cypresses..." | Same with "olive trees" for "oil trees" |
| PNEUMA | "grapevines, fig trees, pomegranates, oaks, evergreens, terebinths, olive trees..." | "Grapevines" and "fig trees" rather than "vines and figs" |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Vines" is the traditional botanical term (vine = grapevine); "figs" not "fig trees" follows Ge'ez. "Olive trees" (LOGOS) is preferable to EMET's "oil trees." PNEUMA's "evergreens" for "ilex" is an over-generalization.

---

**Total disagreements: 5**
